title: Maintaining Proper Pipe Slope for Reliable Drainage
description: Gravity is the primary force moving wastewater through a residential or commercial drainage system. For gravity drainage to function reliably, horizontal drain pipes must maintain a consistent downward slope toward the main sewer or septic connection. If a pipe lacks adequate fall, solid waste settles and causes recurring blockages. Conversely, if the slope is excessively steep, liquid wastewater runs away too fast, leaving heavy solids behind. Maintaining the correct grade specified by local plumbing codes and manufacturer instructions ensures that both liquids and solids transport smoothly through the piping network.
